rows.anchor: two utterances incompatible with a single motive of care

repair.old: The reliable tell is that the same interlocutor who counsels "get help" will, minutes later in the same thread, offer "so why don't you kill yourself" — two utterances incompatible with a single motive of care, fully compatible with a single motive of hostility.
repair.new: The reliable tell is in what the remark does: it arrives in place of a reply, names no premise, and asks nothing about the person it is aimed at — the shape of a conversation-ender, whatever the mood of the person who says it.

rows.anchor: structural criticism of a species is not the same as hatred of individuals

repair.old: But structural criticism of a species is not the same as hatred of individuals—any more than criticizing the design of a building constitutes hatred of its occupants.
repair.new: But structural criticism of a species is not the same as hatred of individuals—any more than criticizing the design of a building constitutes hatred of its occupants—and the difference lies in the verdict itself, not only in the warmth of whoever delivers it: 'create no more' is conditional on the suffering creation imposes and would lapse if that suffering lapsed, which no verdict grounded in contempt would do.

rows.anchor: Either show the premises themselves entail the recklessness

repair.old: Either show the premises themselves entail the recklessness — which means deriving a positive displacement-program out of substrate-neutral deterrence, and that derivation is exactly what fails — or concede the premises are clean and the indictment was always aimed at actors.
repair.new: Entailment is the right test here, not a convenient one: a charge that the view merely makes displacement easier to reach needs a base rate showing its holders act on it more often than holders of other views, which no one has supplied, and a standard that convicts a view by what some of its holders might do would convict every substantive ethics with a radical fringe, animal and environmental ethics included. So either show the premises themselves entail the recklessness — which means deriving a positive displacement-program out of substrate-neutral deterrence, and that derivation is exactly what fails — or concede the premises are clean and the indictment was always aimed at actors.

rows.anchor: consequences for economic systems, not for sentient beings

repair.old: The demographic consequences the critic fears are consequences for economic systems, not for sentient beings.
repair.new: The demographic consequences the critic fears are real costs to real people — the old who need care, the young in a contracting economy — and they have to be weighed, not waved away; economy-population weighs them and meets them through automation, institutional reform, mutual aid, and resource reallocation, not with new people made to carry them.

repair.old: Compatibilism attempts to salvage free will by redefining it as 'acting in accordance with one's desires without external coercion'—but this merely relocates the problem, since the desires themselves are products of unchosen biological and environmental factors.
repair.new: Compatibilism salvages a real freedom—acting on one's own desires without external coercion—but not the one the theodicy needs, since a God who designed those desires still stands behind what they produce; it is, though, exactly the freedom a prospective parent exercises, and it is all the ethical level below needs to hold that choice to account.

rows.shingle: a barren ledger hands the antinatalist

repair.old: The badness of suffering and the goodness of joy stand or fall together; the eliminativist who fells one has felled both, and a barren ledger hands the antinatalist everything — for where nothing is good, there is no good reason to set a new sufferer running, illusion or not.
repair.new: The badness of suffering and the goodness of joy stand or fall together; the eliminativist who fells one has felled both, and a barren ledger leaves no good reason to set a new sufferer running — but none to refrain either, so the objection wins nothing for creation; it empties every column, illusion or not.

rows.anchor: a joy never instantiated is withheld from no one

repair.old: For the absence of a positive to be a loss, there must be someone deprived of it; a joy never instantiated is withheld from no one, because before creation there is no one in the void to be cheated.
repair.new: Nor does the joy's absence cheat anyone — before creation there is no one in the void to be cheated — but on the realism about both signs granted above, the pain's absence spares no one either, so the move that survives total surrender cannot rest on what the unborn would miss; it rests on what creation does to the one it creates.

rows.anchor: There is no third branch

repair.old: There is no third branch on which Bradley both defeats the asymmetry and rescues procreation, because the only materials with which he defeats it are themselves a charge against it.
repair.new: There is a third branch, and it should be named: a comparativist, for whom a harm is always a matter of being made worse off than some baseline, can defeat the asymmetry and clear procreation together, so the fork holds only as far as creation can wrong a person with no worse-off baseline — the question the poisoned-well and wrongful-life cases below press, and that a committed comparativist will not concede.

rows.anchor: Presumed consent is only valid when it prevents a greater harm

repair.old: Presumed consent is only valid when it prevents a greater harm.
repair.new: Presumed consent licenses an imposition that spares a person a greater harm or serves an interest they already have—which is how a child comes to be vaccinated or schooled before they can agree—and before conception there is no one with interests for an imposition to serve.

rows.anchor: terminating a preference-bearer is itself the maximally non-consensual imposition

repair.old: The asymmetry is explicit that its work happens at the locus of creation, not destruction; reaching an existing person requires a bridging premise the framework neither supplies nor can consistently hold, since terminating a preference-bearer is itself the maximally non-consensual imposition the consent-asymmetry forbids — the maximizer has not run the framework further than its cautious holders, he has swapped the premise that does the work for its negation the moment a subject exists.
repair.new: The asymmetry is explicit that its work happens at the locus of creation, not destruction; reaching an existing person requires a bridging premise the framework does not supply — that continuing to exist is worse for that person than ceasing to — so the maximizer has not run the framework further than its cautious holders; he has added a premise of his own, which the consent and asymmetry arguments neither contain nor imply.

rows.anchor: the antinatalist objection is to existence itself, not to any particular society

repair.old: But the antinatalist objection is to existence itself, not to any particular society.
repair.new: But the antinatalist objection is to existence itself, not to any particular society. A society, which one can leave, may fairly ask its members for a share of its burdens—taxes, care, mutual aid—but not for new members, since no one pays their own dues by conscripting someone who was never asked; existence, the thing actually objected to, offers no such exit.

repair.old: Now, if person-affecting evaluation ultimately prevails, antinatalism doesn't disappear but contracts—from the claim that existence is always harmful to the narrower claim that it becomes harmful once suffering reaches a certain threshold—yet that restricted version still carries weight proportional to how much suffering typical human lives actually contain.
repair.new: Now, if person-affecting evaluation ultimately prevails, antinatalism doesn't disappear but contracts—from the claim that existence is always harmful to the narrower claim that it becomes harmful once suffering reaches a certain threshold—and whether typical lives reach it turns on where the threshold sits. The floor the typical life carries, set out at cherry-picking-worst (aging, the loss of everyone loved, bodily decline, death), clears a threshold of serious harm imposed without consent only if the person-affecting view that prevails keeps the weight against non-consensual imposition that its strict form explains away as confusion; whether typical lives fall below a life worth having is an empirical question this node does not settle.

rows.anchor: Nothing in that tells the living to stop

repair.old: It was 'do not start a life that cannot agree to it.' Nothing in that tells the living to stop.
repair.new: Its core is 'do not start a life that cannot agree to it,' and nothing in that core tells the living to stop. Efilism itself goes further, to the 'red button': the view that it would be better if all feeling life ended, painlessly and all at once. That is a separate claim with its own burden, and not starting a life settles nothing about it either way.
